back: Falls in long-run average cost as a firm increases its scale of production.
Rises in long-run average cost when a firm grows beyond its most efficient size.
Technical, purchasing (bulk-buying), marketing, financial, risk-bearing and managerial.
Cost savings from the growth of the industry or area, e.g. skilled labour pool, specialist suppliers, infrastructure, training.
Poor communication, co-ordination and control problems, low motivation in very large firms.
Congestion, higher land prices and rents, competition for scarce skilled workers in a crowded area.
Falls (economies of scale), reaches the most efficient scale, then rises (diseconomies of scale).

front: How do external economies affect the average cost curve?
back: They shift the whole curve downwards; external diseconomies shift it upwards.

front: What falls with economies of scale: total cost or average cost?
back: Average cost. Total cost still rises as output rises.
